conclusion: When first-layer brim width normalization fails, retain the already clipped result produced by support_outside_brim; do not replace it with the unclipped source collection. This lets support interface/contact paths split around the brim instead of restoring an overlapping contour. Continuity is not required, and brim remains enabled with the user's process parameters. The fallback must not add a new geometry pass or an unverified connection across the brim.

sources.locator: normalize_bed_support_widths failure leaves the clipped result intact rather than restoring the unclipped source; make_brim_support_overrides supplies support_outside_brim output
Supplied broken G-code: one first-layer interface has 1.4158252219755514 mm2 actual-bead overlap with brim
Final QQ real-slice check: nine interface segments and zero mm2 actual-bead overlap with two remaining brim paths
Same-model ordinary support control: four first-layer interface paths and zero mm2 overlap with brim

verification.method: Measured intersections between actual extrusion-width bead polygons and the brim in the supplied G-code and the same-model ordinary-support reference. Built the Release application with one worker, sliced only the QQ project through the real CLI, repeated the same overlap measurement and ran Consumer Changed.
verification.summary: The supplied organic first layer had 1.4158252219755514 mm2 of interface/brim overlap; ordinary support on the same model had zero. After retaining the clipped fallback, the actual QQ slice has nine interface segments and zero mm2 overlap, with two brim paths still present. Continuity is not required. The existing width trace still reports center_move_budget, proving the failure path is exercised without enabling diagnostic retention. No other model was used for acceptance and no additional geometry pass was introduced.
